claim:rust-engine-in-workbench.proposition:
The Rust engine runs the bursting gene-expression benchmark as a workbench composite
(RustHybridStep bridging the real run_ir binary) and is ~30-50x faster than plain
interpreted Python per run.

claim:speedup-landscape.proposition:
Rust/numba stays 1.3-2.6x and is nearly flat in event density; the hybrid is faithful to
exact SSA only at stochastic_fraction = 1.0 (where it is the exact path).

claim:regime-frontier.proposition:
No. The only >=5x cells are large systems at low stochastic fraction (10.8x at size 100 /
fraction 0.1; 6.8x at fraction 0.25), and both FAIL fidelity (worst |z| ~14-17). The
faithful cells (stochastic_fraction = 1.0) are ~1.0x. Fast and trustworthy are disjoint.

claim:copy-number-frontier.proposition:
No. The map is FLAT in copy number. At N0 from 20 to 1000, every >=5x cell (stochastic
fraction <= 0.5; 10-11x at fraction 0.1, ~7x at 0.25) FAILS fidelity with worst |z| ~16, and
the value barely moves across a 50x copy-number range. The failure is entirely VARIANCE: the
deterministic mean is faithful at every copy number (worst |z_mean| ~2.5-5, at/below the |z|<=4
gate), but the hybrid gives continuous species ~zero intrinsic variance while exact SSA has
variance ~N0, so worst |z_var| stays ~16 regardless of copy number. The gap is copy-number-
invariant by construction, so copy number was never going to close it. Faithful cells remain
only at stochastic_fraction = 1.0 (fully stochastic, ~1x). 0 of 16 cells are both >=5x and
faithful. This resolves the open decision from regime-frontier and strengthens the
investigation verdict: no faithful-and-fast regime exists even with copy number swept.

narrative.question:
For what kinds of models does a pure-Rust hybrid ODE/SSA engine pay off, and
where does the hybrid partition stay accurate? The viva-hybrid trial measured a
single benchmark (Rust 2.01x vs numba -> MARGINAL); this investigation sweeps
model characteristics to map WHERE a Rust hybrid engine clears the >=5x bar AND
the hybrid approximation remains faithful to exact stochastic simulation.

decisions.title: Adopt a variance-tolerant fidelity criterion (mean-only / relative-variance), or redesign the partition?
decisions.detail:
Copy number has now been swept (20-1000) and does NOT open a faithful-and-fast
window: the >=5x cells fail only on VARIANCE - the deterministic mean is faithful
everywhere. Under the current strict all-species absolute-variance gate (|z|<=4), the
partition's deliberate suppression of continuous-species intrinsic noise is counted as
error at every copy number. For use cases that need only the mean trajectory of the
continuous species (often the whole point of treating them deterministically), the
>=5x region is already mean-faithful. The open decision is whether the next
investigation should (a) evaluate the engine under a mean-only or relative-variance
criterion - which would flip the verdict for those use cases - or (b) test a different
partition / tau-leaping variant that preserves continuous-species variance.
